explanation: The contest that year was held in Brighton, England. The group's name is built from its members' initials: Agnetha, Björn, Benny and Anni-Frid.

claims.text: ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest with the song Waterloo.
Dancing Queen, Mamma Mia and Fernando were not Eurovision entries, so ABBA did not win with any of them.
The Eurovision Song Contest that ABBA won was held in Brighton, England.
The name ABBA is formed from the initials of Agnetha, Björn, Benny and Anni-Frid.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic01w. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for Dancing Queen and Mamma Mia, bigger worldwide hits, which is the trap; neither was a Eurovision entry, and Waterloo is ABBA's one Eurovision win. The stem gives no year because ABBA won once, so the key holds as written. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: ABBA and Eurovision are known worldwide, and the options are four of the group's best-known songs, so players who never watched the contest can still reason from the title. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: None of substance. I kept the year (1974) out of the player text so that every claim is a standard fact about the band.
